purpose: Descriptive only; no normalization or selection
sample_selection: Up to 1024 evenly spaced eligible indices among final control47 replay next-states; nonterminal, finite, >=2 legal next-actions
ensemble_mean: Equal mean per network: 3 or 18+3=21 terms; no equal weighting of differently sized groups
argmax_tie_break: First legal action index, as in numpy.argmax; ties are not evidence of strength
limitations: Training-buffer distribution from one control start only; not representative gameplay or fresh validation. Uses stored next-state masks with next-state features. Raw Q argmax agreement excludes heuristic overrides and does not imply strength. NumPy averaging can differ from runtime Torch reduction near floating-point ties. The replay SHA is captured at diagnostic start, not attested by the training-state schema. Eligible-row sampling also excludes terminal and one-action states; ring-buffer age order is preserved, no independent gameplay sample.
